title: Staged migration runway and TF handoff
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a practical, engineer-first checklist and set of Terraform handoff snippets for running a staged migration of the Private (VPC/on-prem) control plane and runtime. It prioritizes small, reversible changes, observable gates, and an explicit handoff to infra owners for the final TF apply.

Context and goals:
- We need a repeatable sequence for customers upgrading from runtime v2.x -> v3.0 and control plane 5.x -> 6.0 with minimal requests impacted.
- Keep API compatibility surface stable (API shim behavior covered separately) but include confirmation steps.
- Ensure operators can perform a safe rollback at each stage.

High-level phases (short runway):
1) Prep and drift detection (local TF review)
2) Staged infra changes (non-disruptive resource additions)
3) Shadow control plane & runtime registration
4) Traffic split and probes (1% -> 25% -> 100%)
5) Full cutover and deprecation window
6) Post-cutover cleanup and TF consolidation

Pre-flight checklist (must pass before any staged apply):
- Terraform plan runs clean in a dry environment and plan file archived.
- Backups: control plane DB snapshot + runtime state export complete and validated.
- Canary test harness exists for model inference + KV cache preservation.
- Observability hooks: metrics baseline recorded for latency, error rate, token cost.
- Communication: on-call pager for SRE and PM, customer communications draft.

Drift detection and pre-apply review:
- Run terraform plan with -out and save. Compare plans across CI and operator machine.
- Check for any sensitive resource changes (KMS, HSM, network ACLs).
- Operators must explicitly sign-off on any plan that modifies security boundaries.

Staged infra changes (recommended ordering):
A) Add new runtime nodegroup/resource pool (label v3) without draining old nodes
B) Deploy new control plane pods as a shadow set (no leader election for shadow mode)
C) Expose a shadow API endpoint behind internal load balancer for probe traffic

Terraform handoff notes (practical snippets):
- Strategy: break the module into three applies: network -> compute -> control-plane. Keep changes small so a failed apply can be targeted.
- Example snippet pattern (operator-run workflow):
  # run from infra operator host
  terraform init -reconfigure -backend-config=...
  terraform workspace select prod || terraform workspace new prod
  terraform plan -out=plan.preprod.tfplan -var-file=secrets.tfvars
  # operator inspects plan then sign-off (GPG or ticket link)
  terraform apply "plan.preprod.tfplan"

- Module-level tip: add a boolean var enable_shadow_controlplane = false and default false. Toggle true in the compute/control-plane apply step only after nodegroup added.

Compatibility matrix (quick reference):
- runtime v2.x -> v3.0: requires kv-cache migration script (idempotent), model sharding table bump (backwards compatible reads for N hours).
- control plane 5.x -> 6.0: leader election param changed; if leader-election.enabled=false in old cluster ensure new pods start in passive/shadow mode.
- API surface: /v1/generate endpoints are stable; internal admin endpoints changed (admin/v2 -> admin/v3) and require the shim proxy.

Traffic split and validation plan:
- Phase 0 (shadow): route 0% production, run functional probes and load tests against shadow endpoint; assert parity on 95th pct latency +/- 20ms and error-rate delta < 0.1%
- Phase 1 (1%): use smart-reroute in the gateway to send 1% of requests (sticky by user token) for 4 hours; monitor logs and telemetry.
- Phase 2 (25%): increase to 25% with longer soak (24 hours) and run regression evals (prompt sets).
- Phase 3 (100%): switch default routing, keep old control plane in read-only for N hours before tearing down.

Rollback patterns (explicit and easy to run):
- Immediate rollback: flip gateway routing back to old cluster (runbook command provided).
- Partial rollback: scale down v3 nodegroup to zero and re-route to v2. Ensure KV state preserved.
- TF-based rollback: preserve the old tfplan artifact. Do not attempt to reverse-engineer state; instead re-apply the archived plan for the previous stable revision.

Runbook snippets (commands):
- Basic probe (k8s): kubectl --context prod get pods -l app=redwood-runtime -o wide
- Shadow health check (internal LB): curl -H 'X-Redwood-Test: shadow' http://internal-shadow.internal:8080/healthz
- Route flip (gateway shim example): curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' https://gateway.internal/api/v1/routing -d '{"route":"controlplane","target":"v2"}'

Telemetry gating and SLOs to watch:
- P50/P95 latency for generate and chat endpoints
- 5xx rate and per-route error counts
- Cache hit ratio (KV prefix cache) — dropping indicates miss in migration
- Token cost per 1k responses (economic regressions)

Post-cutover cleanup and TF consolidation:
- Keep shadow control plane in read-only for the configured deprecation window (default 72h)
- After stability window, remove enable_shadow_controlplane flags and consolidate modules back into main module tree.
- Archive all tfplans and operator sign-offs into the JIRA ticket for audit.

Testing and rehearsals:
- Run a full dry-run in a dedicated lab that mirrors network ACLs (use replayed p95 traces).
- Chaos injection: simulate node drain and DB failover during 25% soak to validate fallback policies.

Known open questions / TODOs:
- Need a vetted kv-cache migration script that can be run in parallel across heterogeneous hardware; create RFC. (Owner: Marco)
- Confirm HSM key rotation strategy during plan that touches KMS; add explicit step in plan. (Owner: Jillian)
- Provide a small customer-facing communications template for enterprise customers with private deployments. (Owner: Devon)

Notes to self / heuristics:
- Keep TF applies idempotent and short; avoid long-running applies that touch stateful DBs.
- Prefer adding resources first (blue-green) instead of in-place mutation where possible.
- When in doubt, freeze schema changes behind feature flags and flip post-cutover.

Appendix: quick Terraform example for add-nodegroup (copy-paste safe):

resource "redwood_runtime_node_pool" "v3_pool" {
  name        = "runtime-v3-pool"
  instance_type = var.runtime_instance_type
  replicas    = 2
  labels = {
    release = "v3"
  }
  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}

# operator: set var.enable_shadow_controlplane = true in the control_plane apply step to register new control-plane pods without accepting traffic

End of doc.

(Keep as draft until we run two live rehearsals and close the open questions.)
